newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African truth probe looks for army killers.
newsitem.headline: S.African truth probe looks for army killers.

text.p: Members of an apartheid-era hit squad were ordered on Wednesday to testify about their activities, which included trying to intimidate Nobel laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu by nailing a monkey foetus to his door.

Dumisa Ntsebeza, investigative head of South Africa's statutory Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC), said the three would testify behind closed doors in August to the body probing apartheid-era atrocities.

"They are requested in terms of the (National Unity and Reconciliation) Act to give evidence and/or answer questions in relation to various unsolved matters currently under investigation," he said in a statement.

The cynically named Civil Cooperation Bureau (CCB) was set up by the white-led army of the last apartheid government in the 1980s to undermine black resistance groups and intimidate and kill activists.
Run as a private company, it once tried to intimidate Tutu, now chairman of Truth Commission.

The three men, the first officials of the army hit squad to be subpoenaed by the Truth Commission, are former managing director Joe Verster, treasurer Wouter Basson and operative Abram "Snake" van Zyl.
The parents of Namibian human rights lawyer Anton Lubowski blame the CCB for the assassination of their son in 1989.
The TRC has previously used its court-like powers to summon alleged police hit squad members, but has not yet given details of their evidence.
The TRC has received more than 7,000 applications for amnesty for human rights violations in defence of apartheid and in opposition to it.

Vice chairman Alex Boraine said on Wednesday the cut off date for applications would have to be extended beyond the earlier May 10 deadline because parliament had failed to enact legislation required to give certainty about the final deadline.
